title: Private deployments: implement upgrade workflow w/ prechecks, backups, and rollback hooks (VPC + on-prem)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
Deliver a reliable, repeatable upgrade workflow for Redwood Private deployments (VPC + on-prem/air-gapped) with:
1) pre-upgrade safety checks
2) automated backups/snapshots of critical state
3) well-defined rollback hooks + operator UX
4) clear observability + support playbooks

Why
We currently have too many "bespoke" customer upgrade paths that are hard to reproduce and risky under partial failures (failed migrations, image pull failures, mis-detected storage classes). The outcome is longer maintenance windows, higher Support load, and brittle rollback stories.

Scope
- Upgrade orchestration in redwood-private-installer: version selection, step graph/plan output, staged apply, health validation gates, deterministic rollback plan.
- Prechecks framework: cluster readiness (k8s version, node capacity, storage class), schema compatibility checks, secrets/permissions, disk space, config drift detection.
- Backups primitives: control plane DB snapshots + verify, object storage config/state backups, optional PV snapshots, retention guidance.
- Rollback: rollback hooks per component (control plane, runtime, gateways, observability agents), rollback ordering, and downgrade safety constraints (forward-only migrations).
- Packaging + delivery: signed artifacts, upgrade bundles, Helm chart/installer coordination, offline bundle import for air-gapped.
- Ops integration: telemetry for upgrade runs (metrics + structured logs + correlation id), diagnostics bundle generation, runbooks.

Non-goals
- Re-architecting the full private installer from scratch.
- Building a general-purpose GitOps platform.
- Guaranteeing zero downtime across all customer environments (we should minimize downtime and enforce safe sequencing/canaries where possible).

Milestones (target)
Phase 1 (design + policy) [done-ish]
- Finalize upgrade/rollback framework invariants and downgrade policy
- Define compatibility matrix + enforcement mechanism

Phase 2 (implementation) [in progress]
- Installer: pluggable precheck runner + JSON output
- Backup primitive: snapshot DB + verify, wire into upgrade step graph
- Helm hooks/gates: schema migration gating + post-upgrade smoke tests
- Rollback command: re-apply previous known-good versions + restore snapshots where safe
- Offline bundles: import + manifest parsing + signature verification

Phase 3 (hardening + beta)
- Failure injection matrix automated in CI where possible
- Beta with 1–2 Private customers (VPC + on-prem) with comms + support readiness

Phase 4 (GA)
- GA checklist complete (dashboards, runbooks, alert thresholds, support enablement)
- Release notes + change-management process doc updated

Implementation notes / guardrails
- Upgrades must be resumable OR fail closed with an explicit rollback/abort path.
- Any schema migration marked forward-only must block rollback attempts past that boundary (with a clear operator-facing explanation).
- Air-gapped: bundle integrity verification is mandatory; installer must hard-fail on invalid signature/manifest mismatch.
- Operator UX must support both interactive and non-interactive execution (CI / automation); prompts should be bypassable with explicit flags.

Open questions
- "Rollback window" definition for v1 (time-based vs version-based) and how we communicate this to customers.
- PV snapshot scope defaults: opt-in vs required for specific components.
- Performance: backup duration vs maintenance windows; evaluate incremental snapshot option for larger DBs.

Risks
- Partial upgrades leaving deployment in unrecoverable state if health gates are incomplete.
- Downgrade story is constrained by forward-only migrations; need strong precheck messaging + runbook clarity.
- Air-gapped UX + customer-specific security requirements (key custody, signing evidence).

Next steps
- Lock component upgrade ordering and rollback ordering in Helm charts + installer plan output.
- Finish wiring correlation id across installer -> control plane -> runtime logs.
- Run 2 full staging rehearsals (including forced failures) and publish findings to runbook + checklist.
acceptance_criteria:
Functional
- Installer supports an end-to-end upgrade execution path with: prechecks -> backup -> staged apply -> validation gates.
- Installer produces a machine-readable report (JSON) of precheck results, executed steps, timings, and final outcome.
- Rollback is supported for rollback-safe boundaries and refuses to run when blocked by forward-only migrations (with clear messaging).
- Offline bundle import works for air-gapped customers, including signature verification and actionable failure output.

Operational
- Upgrade telemetry exists (metrics + structured logs) with a consistent correlation id.
- Diagnostics bundle can be generated for failed upgrades and includes: precheck report, step graph, timings, relevant k8s events, recent pod logs.
- SRE runbook is complete and validated in a rehearsal; Support escalation checklist is published.

Quality gates
- Failure injection matrix covers at least: disk full, image pull failure, schema mismatch, control plane API unavailable, permission failure on snapshots.
- CI includes at least one automated upgrade/rollback integration test simulating a mid-upgrade failure.

Security
- Signing/verification behavior is implemented for installer artifacts and offline bundles; audit log events emitted for upgrade/rollback actions.

comments: Connor O’Brien (2025-02-05): We should treat this as a release-train feature, not just an installer feature. Need the helm ordering guarantees + control plane version reporting to avoid split-brain upgrades.

Sean Gallagher (2025-02-12): For on-call, the key is: when upgrades fail at 2am, can we quickly answer (a) what step failed (b) whether rollback is safe (c) where the diagnostics bundle is. Please keep "diagnostics bundle" in the critical path for beta.

Marcus Lin (2025-02-20): Please ensure we have auditable events for upgrade/rollback actions (who/when/what). For offline bundles, we need documented key custody + verification behavior and test cases for invalid signatures.
Ethan Park (2025-03-01): +1 to rollback guardrails. Control plane should publish "previous known good" + current component versions to avoid the installer inferring state from k8s resources alone.
